independent_information_justification: Recent Oxford Economic Papers evidence on >150,000 European soccer matches argues that favourite-longshot patterns can arise from imperfect competition and demand elasticity, not only bettor irrationality. Strumbelj also reports bookmaker-level differences in forecast quality. This Issue tests bookmaker-specific margin/allocation signatures directly on matched Football AI fixtures.
issue_title: [AGENT-RESEARCH] 4. BOOKMAKER_MARGIN_STRUCTURE_V1 — сравнить распределение маржи между букмекерами
prohibited: automatic threshold retuning on seen outcomes

required_implementation.evaluator: Add a deterministic Python evaluator that consumes only preregistered allowed inputs and returns machine-readable results.
required_implementation.handler: Add a reviewed Research V5 handler that freezes the protocol before evaluation and writes only inside the current Issue sandbox.
required_implementation.registry: Register the family in research/v5_recipe_registry.json with a bounded max_iterations and the exact no-API safety contract.
required_implementation.tests: Add unit tests for the evaluator/handler and workflow contract tests covering fail-closed safety, temporal/OOS rules, and DONE/CONTINUE state.

research_question: Do different bookmakers systematically distribute 1X2 margin differently across favourites, draws, and longshots on the same football matches, and are those bookmaker-specific patterns stable out of sample?
